title: Restart bluetoothd and reload btusb when the adapter is wedged
head: e1c1b1b938b2
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The now-unconditional bluetoothd restart can leave the user pairing agent unregistered
leads.consequence: On a logged-in machine with the enabled bt-agent.service, restarting bluetooth.service replaces BlueZ's in-memory agent registrations. The current bt-agent only registers at startup. If BlueZ's shutdown Release is not delivered before the bus name disappears, the agent can remain running yet unregistered, and Restart=on-failure will not re-run it. If Release *is* delivered, its handler quits the main loop, then bt-agent tries to UnregisterAgent against a daemon that is stopping or already restarted; an error triggers exit 1 and a systemd retry, while a successful unregister exits 0 and will not restart. Thus a lasting failure depends on shutdown timing; check this with a private D-Bus/systemd fixture or actual authenticated user-service logs before posting as established. Open PR #11937 proposes a supervisor for the BlueZ-owner lifecycle.
leads.triage: behavioural; asked Opus (followup-1 Q3). Source + stand-in test suggest clean restart self-heals; open issue #11936 reports otherwise. Published as hedged 'Related report, not verified'.

leads.summary: Final bluetoothctl list is not bounded by the two-second guard and can hang the menu action
leads.consequence: The successful probe only establishes that bluetoothctl answered then. If bluetoothd disappears after that probe, the second, direct bluetoothctl list is not under timeout and the floating terminal remains stuck, with neither success nor failure. The new test stub always returns immediately and cannot catch this transition.
leads.triage: behavioural; asked Opus (Q1). Confirmed in stub model, pre-existing in PR since first commit, millisecond window. Not published.

leads.summary: An rfkill unblock error can be reported as a successful recovery
leads.consequence: The script does not check rfkill unblock's status. A blocked adapter may still be listed by bluetoothctl, so after a successful service restart the command prints that controller and exits 0 even though the unblock failed. On a failed sudo restart it can additionally print 'Bluetooth is unblocked' when rfkill failed. Gate subsequent work/success on the unblock or report the failure.
leads.triage: behavioural; asked Opus (Q2). rfkill exits nonzero only without /dev/rfkill write access; pre-existing. Folded into N1 wording only.

leads.summary: Open PR #13101 modifies the same Bluetooth restart command and conflicts with this PR
leads.consequence: Both PRs add a service restart to the same old seven-line script. If either merges, the other's head cannot be cleanly merged: Git shows two conflict hunks in the script. Combining both versions naively would run the restart twice or retain #13101's trailing exit $restart_status and bypass this PR's final status. Coordinate or close the duplicate, and resolve in favor of one integrated implementation rather than merging both hunks.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified with gh (#13101 open, same script, same issue) and merge-tree output; Opus re-ran merge-tree during self-check. Published as related note.

leads.summary: A zero or negative restart-wait override skips even the initial probe and reloads a healthy USB driver
leads.consequence: The overridable wait is not validated, and the loop checks the deadline before probing. OMARCHY_BLUETOOTH_RESTART_WAIT=0 (or a negative value) makes wait_for_controller return 1 without calling bluetoothctl; when btusb is loaded, it then unloads and reloads btusb even if the controller was already present. The default 5 is unaffected, but this test-only override is available to callers without an enforced range. Do at least one probe before the deadline check, or reject nonpositive values.
leads.triage: already in Opus final as N4; corroboration. Not published.

limits: H1 remains a hypothesis, not a deterministic loss: BlueZ tag 5.84 and bluez-tools upstream f653217 show the lifecycle and the extra UnregisterAgent call, but a private D-Bus/systemd reproduction is needed to establish how often a Release is delivered and whether a failed unregister causes an automatic restart. No live user bus, adapter or service was queried.

PR #8022 installs an Intel-only rfkill-unblock recovery service that also reloads btusb after five seconds. Concurrent interaction with this manual action was not run under udev/systemd and no deterministic collision is claimed here.

The fetched public omarchy-pkgs PKGBUILDs are the repository's current master with release _commit c668141e, not a recipe frozen to the pinned PR; their bin/* installation loop is only used to establish registration behavior.

flags.claim: A mutant that ignores the failed restart and keeps escalating still passes 10/10.
flags.why: A mutant that ignores the failed restart fails the suite: M3 (exit removed) fails at 'restart bluetooth fails when the service restart fails'. The mutant that passes 10/10 is M4, which records the failure, keeps escalating and still exits 1 before the status. The qualifier 'still exits 1 at the end' was lost.

flags.claim: When sudo succeeds but `systemctl restart` fails, systemd has already stopped bluetoothd before the start fails, so the daemon is now down
flags.why: Holds when the restart job runs and fails in its start phase (restart is patched into a start only after the stop completes). A restart that systemd refuses when building the transaction (masked unit, unit not found, bad unit setting) stops nothing, so 'nothing else was changed' is then true. My own final-report N1 and ledger N1 carry the same absolute wording; this is an inconsistency in my report, corrected here.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed ('restart job fails in its start phase')

flags.claim: That holds when sudo is refused.
flags.why: Read as covering the whole message, it is too strong: 'Bluetooth is unblocked' can be false even when sudo is refused (rfkill unblock without /dev/rfkill write access, or a hard block). The paragraph's last sentence says this, so the two sentences pull against each other. Minor.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed ('The second clause holds when sudo is refused')

flags.claim: `Restart=on-failure` brings it back after about 2 s.
flags.why: systemd was not in the fixture; the restart was modelled by starting a fresh bt-agent, which registered with the successor. Under systemd it also depends on the unit's ExecCondition seeing bluetooth.service active at that moment; an ExecCondition skip is never retried. From source this is normally met (bluetoothd takes its bus name before adapter and agent init), but it is a condition, not a certainty.

flags.claim: #13101's restart lines sit outside the conflict markers, so a quick resolution could keep two restarts and its trailing `exit "$restart_status"`.
flags.why: Checked now (not in my original evidence). The two conflict hunks and the placement of #13101's echo, `sudo systemctl restart bluetooth.service` and `restart_status=$?` outside the markers are correct (merged lines 39-41). But `exit "$restart_status"` is inside the second hunk, on #13101's side (merged line 92). So it survives only if that side is kept, while the restart lines survive any choice of sides. 'could keep' keeps the sentence from being wrong; the 'so' ties both to 'outside the markers', which is imprecise. Minor.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed (trailing exit tied to keeping both sides of hunk 2)

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13085#issuecomment-5826234034) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13085#issuecomment-5839486366), checked at `e1c1b1b`.

**Verified:** all five points from the earlier review are resolved on this head. The two-controller scope note is unchanged, as intended. None of the earlier points turned out wrong. The updated description matches the code: the flow diagram, the ten test names, the failure of the suite against the upstream script, and the mutation control (`sudo modprobe -r btusb && sudo modprobe btusb` now fails the suite).

| Earlier point | Result at `e1c1b1b` (sandbox, privileged commands stubbed) |
|---|---|
| Failed restart could end in success | Resolved. Sudo denied with a controller listed: exit 1 after 1 sudo call (previous head: exit 0). Sudo denied, no controller: 1 sudo call and exit 1 at once (previous head: 3 calls over 20 s). |
| Restart runs on every invocation | Resolved. The description and the script comment now state that the restart is unconditional and why. |
| 5 s window stretched without a daemon | Resolved. Unit inactive after restart: exit 1 in under 0.01 s with no probes (previous head: 35 s). Daemon up, no controller: about 5 s, reload, about 15 s, exit 1. |
| Failure hint | Resolved. Points at `journalctl -b -k`, names the daemon's log separately, no `lsusb`. The suite now checks it. |
| Busy-module test | Resolved. The stub fails `-r`; the script reports the failed unload and skips the load. |
| Two-controller scope | Unchanged by design. |

The `systemctl is-active` gate does not block the #12519 recovery: `/sys/class/bluetooth` is registered when `bluetooth.ko` initialises, and `btusb` depends on it, so the unit's condition can only be unmet when `btusb` is not loaded.

Two small points on the new code, plus two related notes.

### The restart-failure message can be inaccurate

When the restart fails, the script prints `Could not restart bluetooth.service. Bluetooth is unblocked; nothing else was changed.` The second clause holds when sudo is refused. When sudo succeeds but the restart job fails in its start phase, systemd has already stopped bluetoothd, so the daemon is now down (systemd `job.c`: a restart runs as stop, then start; the stubbed run shows the same message on this path). "Bluetooth is unblocked" is also not guaranteed: `rfkill unblock` exits 0 under a hard block, and its failure (no write access to `/dev/rfkill`) is not checked.

**Impact:** on a failed restart, the message can say nothing changed while bluetoothd has been stopped.

**Suggested change:** drop the second sentence, or replace it with the `systemctl status bluetooth.service` hint the `is-active` branch already prints.

**Optional test improvement:** the assertion `restart bluetooth stops before btusb when the restart failed` cannot fail. The sudo stub fails every call, so no `modprobe` can be logged, and the case already lists a controller, so the reload branch is never reached. A mutant that keeps escalating after the failed restart and only exits 1 at the end still passes 10/10. Logging sudo calls in the stub, running this case with no controller listed, and asserting exactly one sudo call would make it test what its name says.

**Related open PR:** #13101 also adds a `bluetooth.service` restart to this script for #13078. Merging this PR's head and #13101's head against their common base (`git merge-tree`) gives two conflict hunks in `bin/omarchy-restart-bluetooth`, and #13101's unchecked restart lines sit outside the conflict markers, so any resolution keeps them next to this PR's restart. Keeping both sides of the second hunk would also keep #13101's trailing `exit "$restart_status"`.

**Related report, not verified:** open issue #11936 (BlueZ 5.87) reports that after `systemctl restart bluetooth.service`, `bt-agent.service` stays running with the same PID but unregistered, so pairing fails with "No agent available". This action now restarts bluetoothd on every use. Source reading and a test of the real `bt-agent` against a stand-in BlueZ on a private bus point the other way for a clean stop: bluetoothd sends `Release`, bt-agent's follow-up `UnregisterAgent` fails, it exits 1, and `Restart=on-failure` brings it back after about 2 s, provided `bluetooth.service` is active again by then (the unit's `ExecCondition`). A stale agent appeared only when the stand-in exited without sending `Release` (as after a crash or SIGKILL). One check on hardware would settle it: after running the menu action, `journalctl --user -b -u bt-agent` should show `Agent released` followed by a new registration.

Source reading of the script, test, menu entry and `bt-agent.service`, plus BlueZ 5.87, systemd v262, kmod 34.2, util-linux, bash 5.3, Linux 7.2 and bluez-tools source.
